clinicalHistory: 5-year-old with suspected peanut allergy after facial swelling at a birthday party; referred for skin-prick testing to confirm sensitisation.
allergensTested: Peanut, tree nut mix, egg, cow's milk
whealSizes: Peanut 12mm, tree nut mix 3mm, egg 2mm, cow's milk 0mm; positive control 6mm, negative control 0mm
interpretation: Marked peanut skin-prick weal with a systemic reaction (facial angioedema, wheeze, and hypotension) developing during testing, requiring immediate treatment with intramuscular adrenaline and observation.
impression: Confirmed peanut sensitisation with a severe systemic reaction during in-vivo testing.
recommendedFollowUp: Urgent allergy/immunology review, adrenaline auto-injector prescription and training, strict peanut avoidance advice.
clinicianNotes: Resuscitation trolley used; patient observed for 4 hours post-reaction and discharged well.
